newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP Q3 not as good as appears-analysts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP Q3 not as good as appears-analysts.

text.p: Australian mining analysts said on Friday that early analysis of the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's (BHP) third quarter profit indicated the result may not be as strong as it appeared on the surface.
BHP reported a net profit of A$378 million for the three months to February 28, compared with A$223 million for the previous corresponding quarter.
"The result does not appear to be as good as the first cut shows," said a Melbourne-based analyst, who declined to be named.

"There is some asset sales and tax adjustments in the A$378 million number and that brings it back towards the A$330-340 million level, which is probably a bit below the market's expectations," the analyst said.
A Sydney-based analyst, who also declined to be named, agreed, saying he believed the underlying result fell below market expectations.
"I think that the underlying result is lower than the reported number and quite substantially," he said.
But analysts said that even so, this did not explain the fall in BHP's share price after the release of the results.
They said it was more likely that the drop was related to profit-taking and weakness in the major offshore stock markets on Thursday.
"The market has pushed it (BHP) up over the last few days, having heard a rumour of a great result," one analyst said.
"It was a good result, but perhaps not as good as some of the rumour-mongers in the market had expected."
At 1.10 p.m. (0210 GMT), BHP shares were two cents lower at A$17.11 after trading as high as A$17.32 before the result and off a low of A$17.05 after the result.
